title: Full, conscious, active (Sacrosanctum Concilium 14)
hook: the council's hope for how everyone takes part
tomorrow: who is the Church's light really for?

segments.voice: Yesterday, summit and font: the week climbs toward the altar, and the altar sends it back out. The line was summit and font.

At a concert there's the crowd that sings every word, and the crowd that films it. Same song, same room, two different nights. At Mass the priest leads the prayers, the choir sings, a reader takes the ambo. So what's left for the person halfway back in the pew, holding a coat? In paragraph fourteen of its document on the liturgy, the council answers with three words, and they ask a lot.
screen: `SING IT, OR FILM IT?` → `WHAT'S LEFT FOR THE PEW?` → `THREE WORDS.`

segments.voice: First, the hope. The council says Mother Church earnestly desires that all the faithful be led to full, conscious and active participation in the liturgy. Full: the whole person, not a corner of the attention. Conscious: knowing what's happening and meaning it. Active: actually taking part. The reason is baptism. The council quotes First Peter: "a chosen generation, a kingly priesthood, a holy nation, a purchased people." Taking part is the baptized people's right and their duty. Second, what active looks like. A later paragraph, number thirty, lists acclamations, responses, psalms and songs, gestures and postures, and then a surprise: at the proper times, a reverent silence. Active includes being still on purpose. Third, a neighbor who prizes the same thing, in its own words. In a synagogue, when the Kaddish is said, the congregation answers together in Aramaic: amen, may his great name be blessed. The Talmud, in the tractate Shabbat, teaches that whoever answers that amen with all their strength has a harsh decree against them torn up. Both ask the people in the seats for more than being there: their whole voice. Fourth, one honest difference. In the synagogue, that answer centers on praising God's name. At Mass, the responses gather around the altar and the Eucharist, which Catholics believe is Christ's body. Neither is a copy of the other.
screen: `FULL, CONSCIOUS, ACTIVE.` · `SILENCE IS ON THE LIST.` · `AMEN, WITH ALL YOUR STRENGTH.` · `TWO CENTERS, ONE WHOLE VOICE.` · then, large: `FULL AND ACTIVE.`

segments.voice: Sit as you might in a pew, feet down, hands at rest. Say one response aloud, the way a congregation does, Amen or Thanks be to God, and mean every syllable. Then keep a reverent silence, the kind the council counts as taking part.
Full. The first of the council's three words for how everyone takes part in the liturgy: the whole person, present. Today's word.
Your line: full and active. On the council's list, even the silence counts. That's today.

howItsDone: At Mass, Catholics in the pews sing, say the responses and acclamations, stand, sit and kneel together, and keep moments of silence; in a synagogue, the congregation answers the Kaddish together.

notes: SC 14 and SC 30 paraphrased (official English not public domain): confirm 'Mother Church earnestly desires', 'full, conscious, and active participation', 'right and duty by reason of their baptism', and SC 30's list ending with reverent silence at the proper times. SC 14's 'primary and indispensable source' sentence was cut for length.
SC 14 quotes 1 Peter 2:9 from the Vulgate; the script quotes the Douay-Rheims wording: confirm.

Unity thread (wisdom day): Shabbat 119b paraphrased: whoever answers 'Amen, yehei shmei rabba' (may His great name be blessed) with all his strength, his harsh decree is torn up (some read 'with all his might', others 'with full concentration'). A Jewish reader should confirm the paraphrase, the tractate reference, and that the Kaddish response is described accurately (it is said in Aramaic, answered by the congregation).

Honest difference voiced without ranking: the Kaddish response centers on praising God's name; the Mass responses gather around the altar and the Eucharist. 'Neither is a copy of the other' guards against 'all the same'.
The concert image is the script's.
Original game: 'actuosa participatio' from SC 14's Latin (actuosam participationem); confirm pronunciation with a Latinist.
